_comment: Ceilings and baseline consumed by verify-deploy.sh Gate 20 (orchestrator context budget lock). Two per-file ceilings are fixed/reviewed PATH.md-derived targets (not headroom-derived from measured_bytes, unlike claudemd-size-budget.json's formula). As of 2026-09-18 both tracked files are under their ceiling (see each file's own derivation for history); ORCHESTRATOR_BUDGET_GATE_MODE remains warn-tier as a recorded follow-up -- promoting it to hard is deferred until commands/orchestrate.md settles past the concurrent sibling task editing it this cycle, since any of that sibling's growth would otherwise become a hard deploy failure. eager_load.baseline_bytes is a fixed historical record (2026-09-02) copied verbatim from the task description that introduced this gate -- re-measure with 'REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash scripts/measure-eager-context.sh --check' and re-derive only baseline_bytes deliberately (it is the regression ceiling, not a rolling target); measured_bytes/measured_at fields are informational snapshots and may be refreshed freely.

skills/skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md.derivation: PATH.md 'Budgets' target ceiling. Grew to 21,318 B (over ceiling) via a 2026-09-18 D4 message-findings-recovery documentation commit that restated content already present in docs/architecture/handoff-schema.md's 'Postflight Boundary' section and context/standards/postflight-tool-restrictions.md. Resolved same day by collapsing that restatement to pointers (Postflight Boundary D4 paragraph, Move 3 bash comments) plus a wording-economy pass over several other paragraphs already covered by orchestrate-state-machine.md/handoff-schema.md -- no operational content removed. Trimmed to 19,535 B measured via wc -c, back under ceiling with ~465 B headroom.

commands/orchestrate.md.derivation: Original PATH.md 'Budgets' target was 8,000 B; unreachable without relocating this file's ~10 KB STAGE 0 executable bash block, which is out of scope (a code-relocation change, not a documentation trim). Growth history: 15,812 B (2026-09-07) -> 19,967 B (2026-09-18, focus-prompt/forced-phase/cycle-budget documentation task) -> 20,228 B (2026-09-18, same-day sibling task's batch-orchestration-default documentation landing two more pointer lines). Reviewed, dated ceiling move: final measured size (20,228 B) + 500 B, rounded up to the next 500 B = 21,000 B. A restatement trim of the Options table's --fast/--research/--plan/--implement rows and the forced-phase Constraints bullet (duplicating docs/architecture/orchestrate-state-machine.md) remains available as a future follow-up once the file is not concurrently claimed by another in-flight task.

eager_load.note: Regression check fails ABOVE baseline_bytes (via 'REPO_ROOT=$(pwd) bash scripts/measure-eager-context.sh --check', parsing the 'TOTAL: <bytes> B' line). baseline_bytes is a fixed recorded ceiling and must never be silently re-derived from a fresh measurement -- only a deliberate, reviewed change should move it. Deliberately bumped from 64450 to 65950 (2026-09-18, focus-prompt/forced-phase/cycle-budget documentation-consistency task): merge-sources/claudemd.md's `/orchestrate` command-table row (predicted-assembled into CLAUDE.md, hence eagerly loaded) grew to document three corrected behaviors -- the per-run work-cycle budget contract (no more `--continue-budget`), artifact-keyed forced plan/implement admission, and the `$2+` user-focus-string threading into dispatched agents' `User focus:` blocks -- growing the eager total from 64,394 B to 65,889 B measured. The new baseline carries a small (~61 B) margin above the measured total rather than pinning it exactly, consistent with the prior baseline/measured gap. CORRECTED 2026-09-21: the previously recorded 66,026 B figure (76 B over baseline) did not reproduce -- re-measuring fresh, and again after checking out the exact commit that originally recorded it, both yield 65,257 B, not 66,026 B. The live eager-load total is 65,257 B, 693 B under baseline_bytes (65,950 B). baseline_bytes remains unmoved because there is no reproduced regression to justify moving it; the 66,026 B figure is treated as a stale/erroneous prior measurement rather than a real event to re-baseline against.
